STAR-4612.notes: The mirror target is the EXISTING workflow seed directory, deliberately NOT the agent-readable canon mirror tree — agents compose from the DB and must not read stale workflow files; the mirror exists purely so a definition change becomes a reviewable commit. Making the export payload identical to the seeder schema is what buys round-trip fidelity almost free and leaves the seeder untouched. FOUR HAZARDS, each a silent corruption: (1) a mode's ordered step-slug list is what the composer executes — it ignores each step's own sort_order, so sorting on serialize reorders every workflow; (2) the seeder read workflow-level meta but NOT step/mode meta while a meta.lean flag decides whether compose inlines step bodies or emits a fetch-on-demand index — emitting meta without teaching the seeder to read it breaks fidelity and changes agent behaviour (source fixed the seeder); (3) workflows sit on a non-default connection so the importer names it explicitly — a bare transaction helper wraps nothing; (4) children are upserted by (workflow_id, slug), not deleted and recreated as the seeder does, so ids stay stable and a re-import cannot destroy live edits. TESTING NOTE: the source's determinism test (identical bytes between consecutive syncs) is what makes the nightly drift PR meaningful — a non-deterministic serializer opens a PR every night against an unchanged DB and reviewers learn to ignore it. Also: Http::fake() MERGES stubs, so a test needing two different responses for one URL must use a sequence, not two fake() calls. The source's seeder docblock claimed the files were a one-time bootstrap that nothing regenerates — that becomes false and must be corrected in the same change, or the next reader believes the generated files are hand-authored.

STAR-4622.notes:
STAGED AT THE USER'S EXPLICIT DIRECTION over a recommendation to hold. The design tension is genuine and is written into the task's Context section: the target already achieves parallel work via git worktrees that all bind-mount into a SINGLE container set (which is why its worktree script insists worktrees live under a specific directory). Per-instance compose is a SECOND, competing isolation mechanism. If both are to coexist, the boundary needs stating — worktrees for parallel branches sharing one stack and one database; separate instances for divergent database state. HARD-WON LESSON from the source: parametrizing container names creates a repo-wide invariant with NO enforcement, and it drifted for months — 41 hardcoded occurrences accumulated across docs, scripts, workflow definitions and live DB records, including one that told agents to read migration status from a different checkout. If this is adopted, land a pre-commit gate against hardcoded container names IN THE SAME CHANGE, with documented exemptions for text that quotes the anti-pattern inside a warning and for deploy files where the fixed name is the real container_name.

2026-07-21 UPDATE — the source completed the epic this entry was staged from, and the lesson above was borne out and then closed out. What the target should take:
(1) THE GATE IS THE DELIVERABLE. The 41-occurrence drift happened because the invariant had no enforcement. check-container-names.sh now covers three forms with the SAME failure mode -- a name anywhere (not just after `docker exec`), a clone host:port, and either of those as a config value/default or in a doc. Scoped to changed LINES, not files, so pre-existing occurrences in docs don't fail someone touching them for unrelated reasons.
(2) PREFER DELETING container_name TO PARAMETERIZING IT. The source had to parameterize because its deploy renames a fixed container and routes a tunnel at it. VERIFIED 2026-07-21 that the target has no such constraint: its ci/ has zero container_name or `docker compose` references and its deploy is an atomic filesystem-layout swap. So the target can drop the names outright and let COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME namespace them -- strictly better, since there is then no variable to leave unset. Do NOT copy the ${INSTANCE_NAME}-* parameterization; it is the source's workaround for a constraint the target does not have. This divergence is NOT a backport candidate -- it is not feedable back, because the source's constraint is real. Recorded in differences.md so a later run does not try to converge them.
(3) THE HARDCODES ARE NOT ONLY IN CODE. The final increment found them in the agent rules canon and in the DB workflow definitions -- including a ship gate that sent every agent to one fixed clone, so the 'verified in a running app' criterion could be satisfied against code the agent never edited, and pass. Whatever the target's equivalent DB-owned instruction surfaces are, sweep them too; a repo-only grep will report clean while the live instructions still pin a clone.
(4) A GENERATED MIRROR IS FIXED AT ITS SOURCE. Both the canon and workflow mirrors are exempted by prefix in the gate, because editing the mirror is itself the defect.
(5) VERIFIED TARGET DEFECTS as of origin/develop ed809baf61, written into the task: 8 hardcoded container_name in docker-compose.yml; docker-compose.override.yml gitignored and hand-written per checkout (scripts/worktree symlinks it into each worktree, propagating the workaround); scripts/shell/aliases.sh:48,51 run the quality gates via `docker exec -t starship-quality`, which from any other checkout reports green for a tree it never read.

AB-2420.notes:
Seed spectrum + priced resolver + reseed. worktree-db.php is 534 lines of standalone PHP (no Laravel) run inside the app container; its header carries the design argument. Exit codes 0=within budget / 1=over / 2=usage-or-connection, deliberately distinct.

Seed = BASE (every table under a small size threshold -- where reference/lookup data lives) + CLOSURE (transitive FK PARENT set), then `coherentBase()` PRUNES to a fixed point: a base table whose parent is not in the seed is dropped, and dropping one can orphan another. Prune rather than close, because the parents involved are the largest tables and every worktree would otherwise pay for a table it never asked for. Matters because mariadb-dump loads with FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0, so orphan rows load silently and surface later as a null relation.

Other details: envValue() must parse .env directly (the container exports no DB_*, so getenv() alone authenticates with an empty password); sizes read live from information_schema because the schema grows; closure BFS needs a seen-set because FK cycles exist; budgetBytes() must REFUSE a bare/non-numeric --budget-mb (it would parse to 0/1 and reject every seed); reportOverBudget falls back to the whole seed when seed-minus-base is empty, so it never promises culprits and names none.

reseed ORDER is the whole point: resolve the new spec BEFORE dropping, or a typo'd table destroys the schema and then aborts, leaving no database. Rebuild rather than top up (a partial add leaves rows whose parents were never copied). reseed also PROMOTES a `none` worktree.

`none` refused for a migration-adding branch (git diff --diff-filter=A <base> -- database/migrations); the refusal PROVISIONS rather than failing.

ALEPHBEIS DIVERGENCE (deliberate, decided at staging): price/budget the MySQL side only and treat pgsql as always-full -- the pg side is new code and tiny, and making the agent reason about it buys nothing. Say so in the resolver output.

Asset staleness stamp (branch@sha + recipe + time); rebuild triggers include `find <inputs> -newer <stamp>` with NO -type f so a branch that only DELETES frontend files is caught via directory mtimes; an unstamped bundle is always replaced. AB-2423.notes:
--watch live rebuild + the verification staleness protocol. The staleness reasoning is the valuable part and is written up at length in .agents/reference/worktrees.md under 'Watching a worktree while an agent works on it'.

THE TEST: each bundle's newest build STARTED after the newest edit to THAT BUNDLE'S OWN inputs, and has finished. Started-not-finished, because a build already running when an edit lands finishes after it while not containing it. PER BUNDLE, because bundles sharing an input let the fast one vouch for the slow one -- measured at 590ms of false green -- and worse, vite does not reliably queue a rebuild for an edit landing mid-build, leaving a bundle stale indefinitely behind a reading that says current. Per-bundle turns that into a refusal, which is the honest answer.

Record lives OUTSIDE public/build (vite empties that every rebuild). Timestamps are file MTIMES, never written clock values -- BusyBox date has no sub-second format and a whole-second stamp cannot be compared against a source edited later in the same second.

Watcher process: PID 1 so it MUST install a TERM/INT handler or docker stop waits the full grace period then SIGKILLs; touch the started markers BEFORE launching (the first build prints no 'build started'); VITE_KEEP_OUT_DIR flag read by vite config as emptyOutDir: env !== '1' (vite empties public/build on EVERY rebuild, manifest included, so a refresh mid-rebuild is a 500 not a page); watchdog exits if either bundle process dies (liveness is read from the CONTAINER, so a half-dead watcher would advertise rebuilds it is not doing); the watcher REWRITES the stamp rather than touching it (the stamp is inside the directory vite empties, and the container has no git -- pass branch/sha as env).

Arbitration: serve WITHOUT --watch stands any watcher down (so an agent verifying never inherits watch mode); stop_watcher removes the record UNCONDITIONALLY including when no container remains (a watcher that exits on its own leaves a STOPPED container, and gating on 'is it running' strands the marker -- and the refusal message names stop as the remedy, which would then do nothing); the 'watching' marker is written only ONCE A BUILD HAS LANDED; the watcher must NOT write the artifact that stands as proof a build finished, because it cannot honestly assert that.

4b25377e96 is the later fix letting verification and a live watcher share a worktree without a redundant build.

ALEPHBEIS: the consumer is the frontend-testing workflow / Playwright path, not scripts/verify -- adapt the waiting+refusal contract to whatever performs browser verification here.

Worktrees share one .git, so --branches lists every local branch in the repo including every squash-merged branch whose remote was deleted (unpushed forever). node CLI resolver + stop cloning node_modules. INVESTIGATED AND CONFIRMED AT STAGING, because the two projects' canon docs give contradictory instructions and only one can be right.

Finding: alephbeis clones node_modules because grumphp.yml sets `eslint: bin: node_modules/.bin/eslint` -- a LITERAL RELATIVE PATH resolved against cwd, which does not exist in a worktree. That is NOT a Node module-resolution problem: worktrees live inside the checkout and Node walks UP, so the checkout's tree is already found (the eslint config's own plugin imports resolve that way today). The clone is a workaround for one hardcoded path, and it costs a full dependency tree per worktree plus invisible staleness (a local copy shadows the real one and is nobody's staleness input).

Tells checkout from worktree WITHOUT git on PATH: a worktree's .git is a FILE, the checkout's is a DIRECTORY. Error text special-cases */.claude/worktrees/* to say a worktree holds no packages of its own.

f07da98903 is the doc-correction commit that also fixed the node_modules guidance.

The asymmetry to write into canon, because it looks arbitrary: vendor MUST be a local copy (PHP resolves __DIR__ through symlinks, so a shared vendor points the PSR-4 map at the checkout's app/ and every worktree edit is silently ignored); node_modules must NOT be copied (Node resolves upward and finds it anyway). Same word, opposite answers, for language-specific reasons.

Note also the two-trees problem the source documents: the frontend service mounts a named volume over node_modules while a host-side asset build resolves the host tree; they agree only while someone installs in both. Alephbeis has the same shape (frontend_node_modules volume).

A clean checkout is always a known-good tree to build from, serve from and diff against; nothing done to a branch can strand it; git status there answers a question rather than showing somebody's WIP. Source implementation is RuleContentPatcher, ~58 lines, a plain final Service consumed by UpdateRuleAction. STO-923.notes: Stands alone — no dependency on the reflection design. Purpose is a GROUP BY, not forensics: 'which tool did somebody reach for when none of them fitted'. Deliberately stores NO arguments and NO results (a tool argument carries personal data and the table has no consent story or retention policy); error truncated because 'a database error can embed the statement that failed along with its bindings'. Outcomes: unknown_tool, refused, forwarded, preview (recorded ok:true — 'a preview is not a failure and must not read as one'), not_callable, ran, unauthorized. Every write fire-and-forget with the rejection swallowed: 'a bridge that refused a call because it could not write a row would turn a reporting problem into an outage.' spaceId taken only when it looks like a uuid. stopal already has McpAuth.tokenId annotated 'useful for audit logs' and read by nothing.

STO-925.notes: stopal's live hazard: scripts/sync/mcp/common.sh + .agents/config/mcp.json.example carry ONE hardcoded https://stopal.app/mcp, copied verbatim by new-instance.sh into every checkout — so every agent session everywhere writes to PRODUCTION silently and a local /mcp is unreachable. Part 1 (per-checkout endpoint derived from the checkout's own port) is small, urgent, and independent; doctrine 7 already says a -local MCP server is registered per project with its URL derived from APP_URL, never in a global registry. Part 2 = the election. Load-bearing properties: held server-side against the TOKEN not the person; lapses; read ONCE per call and passed down (re-reading opens a window where the gate finds no production target while the routing that follows does, and forwards an unacknowledged write); an unhonourable pin is reported IN THE ANSWER to the call that wanted it; a platform-declared tool is REFUSED, never downgraded. The production-confirm gate fires only on write AND target=production AND via='switch' — a caller with no clone would otherwise meet the word on every write, 'which is exactly how it stops being read'. FULL adanim MCP survey (reflection, visibility, forwarding, router) is in this session's transcript; only the election/endpoint half is staged.
